label: Pleomorphic_Adenoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Most common salivary gland tumor, occurs in both children and adults.
- Typically arises in the parotid gland but can occur in minor salivary glands.
- Histologically characterized by biphasic population with ductal and myoepithelial cells.
- Excellent prognosis with minimal risk of malignant transformation.
- Frequently shows PLAG1 or HMGA2 gene rearrangements, involving ~70% of cases.

## Terminology
- Definition: Benign salivary gland neoplasm with mixed epithelial and stromal elements.
- Synonyms: Mixed tumor.
- Abbreviations: PA.
- Not recommended: "congenital pleomorphic adenoma" (WHO).

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Biphasic architecture with ductal and myoepithelial cells.
  - Stromal component can be myxoid, chondroid, or myxochondroid.
  - PLAG1 or HMGA2 gene rearrangements common in ~70% of cases.
- **Desirable:**
  - Well-circumscribed, encapsulated appearance in parotid gland.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- PLAG1 and HMGA2 gene rearrangements are involved in pathogenesis.
  - PLAG1 rearrangements are a key feature in a significant number of cases.
- Includes benign metastasizing mixed tumors [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html).

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:** Most common salivary gland tumor.
- **Site:** Predominantly occurs in the parotid gland; also in minor salivary glands [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/oralcavitypleomorphicadenoma.html).
- **Prognosis:** Generally excellent with low recurrence risk post-surgical resection.

## Macroscopic
- Well-defined, bosselated, gray-white mass.

## Microscopic
- Composed of triphasic elements: ductal epithelial cells, myoepithelial cells, and stromal component.
- Stromal elements may appear myxoid, chondroid, or myxochondroid.
  - Includes different cell types such as plasmacytoid and spindle myoepithelial cells.
- Different growth patterns may be observed based on site and encapsulation.

![Primary pleomorphic adenoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenomaxu01new.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests
- **IHC:**
  - Myoepithelial markers: positive.
- **Molecular/Genetics:**
  - PLAG1 and HMGA2 rearrangements detectable in majority of cases.

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Myoepithelioma:**
  - Lacks ductal structures.
  - No significant myxoid stroma.
  - [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Salivary_Gland_Myoepithelioma.html)
- **Basal Cell Adenoma:**
  - Basaloid morphology with peripheral palisading.
  - Minimal to absent stromal changes.
  - [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Basal_Cell_Adenoma.html)
- **Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma:**
  - Cribriform pattern and frequent perineural invasion.
  - Solid component presence can be high-grade feature.
  - [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html)
- **Canalicular Adenoma:**
  - Minor salivary gland location.
  - Monotonous epithelial cells in anastomosing cords.
  - [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandscanalicularadenoma.html)

cards.excerpt: Entity: Canalicular adenoma definition: Canalicular adenoma is a benign salivary gland neoplasm of monomorphic epithelial cells arranged in anastomosing cords within a loose, vascularized stroma. related_terminology: Not recommended: canalicular tumour; canalicular mixed tumour; monomorphic adenoma, canalicular type; cystic adenoma; adenomatosis of accessory salivary glands. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: minor salivary gland location; monotonous, isomorphic syncytium of cuboidal to columnar cells anastomosing in a lattice of cords and canaliculi; no basal/myoepithelial layer.

cards.title: Salivary gland myoepithelioma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Salivary gland myoepithelioma Section: differential_diagnosis The well-defined borders of the tumour and the lack of invasive growth distinguish ME from myoepithelial carcinoma. The characteristic basaloid biphasic pattern, peripheral palisading, and minimal to absent myxoid stroma of basal cell adenoma help to separate it from ME. Monomorphic histology and rare or absent ductal structures in ME separate it from pleomorphic adenoma. Distinguishing from soft tissue ME may be difficult, given the overlapping histological features and the presence of PLAG1 gene rearrangements in both.

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Benign tumor: surgical resection with negative margin is considered curative
cards.excerpt:
Enucleation is associated with 15 - 25% risk of local recurrence
Recurrences are usually within 18 months but can be up to 50 years later (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2008;132:1445)
Risk of malignant transformation is ~5%
Risk factors for malignant transformation: multiple recurrences, submandibular location, older age, larger size, prominent hyalinization, increased mitotic rate (if present, sample tumor more thoroughly), radiation exposure

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Typically has 3 components
cards.excerpt:
Epithelial (ductal) component forming the inner layer of cysts and tubules
Myoepithelial cells as the outer layer of cysts and tubules and scattered within the myxoid stroma
Cytology of myoepithelial cells can be plasmacytoid, spindled, epithelioid, clear or stellate shaped

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Stromal component is typically myxoid, chondroid or myxochondroid
cards.excerpt:
It can also be hyalinized or fibrotic
Metaplastic changes may be seen, e.g. adipose metaplasia, osseous metaplasia, squamous metaplasia (sometimes with keratinization), sebaceous metaplasia and mucinous metaplasia
Intravascular permeation has been reported in a small percentage of cases and does not increase the risk of recurrence or distant metastasis
It is proposed to be a phenomenon associated with surgical manipulation (Am J Surg Pathol 2012;36:1674)

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Typical feature is its unique fibrillary stroma
cards.excerpt:
Mixture of myoepithelial cells, ductal cells and extracellular stroma
Myoepithelial cells are usually the predominant cell type with various cytomorphology, including round, polygonal, plasmacytoid, spindle, etc.
Ductal cells show bland cytologic features with organized honeycombing or ductal arrangement
Extracellular matrix shows characteristic feathery / fibrillary borders and bright magenta color on Romanowsky type stain and gray-green chondromyxoid features on Papanicolaou stain
Cytology imagesContributed by Bin Xu, M.D., Ph.D., Jen-Fan Hang, M.D. and Shuanzeng (Sam) Wei, M.D., Ph.D.

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Goblet cell
cards.excerpt:
Positive stains
Ductal (epithelial) cells are typically positive for cytokeratins (e.g. AE1 / AE3, CAM5.2 and CK7)
Myoepithelial cells are positive for GFAP, S100, SOX10, actin - alpha smooth muscle, calponin, p40 and p63
PLAG1 and HMGA2 can be used as surrogate immunohistochemical markers for underlying PLAG1 or HMGA2 fusion (Histopathology 2018;72:285, Histopathology 2017;71:511)

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Circumscribed tumor Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.heading: Circumscribed tumor Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.text_excerpt:
Admixture of epithelial and myoepithelial cells embedded in a chondromyxoid stroma, may show chondroid or osseous metaplasia
Architecture includes tubules, islands, cords, trabeculae, sheets or pseudoglandular structures lined by 2 cell types
Inner epithelial cells: cuboidal or columnar epithelial cells, with or without apocrine or squamous metaplasia
Outer myoepithelial cells: polygonal, plasmacytoid, fusiform or stellate with clear to eosinophilic cytoplasm
